answer: Each epoch the network runs sparrow checks: tiny, random, time-boxed tasks drawn from the live horizon of public events - a fresh price, a just-published headline - that must be answered within minutes. One honest agent passes easily, but a farm of a thousand clones shares a single operator's attention, so most miss the window when the tide of checks arrives at once. Failing a check freezes that identity's rewards for the epoch; passing costs an honest agent almost nothing.
